question_text: A 62-year-old man presents to the ED complaining of severe eye pain that started a few hours ago. The patient reports that he fell asleep while watching TV on the couch and woke up with right-sided eye pain and blurry vision. His wife drove him to the emergency room. His wife reports that since they arrived the patient has also been complaining of intense nausea. The patient denies fever, headache, or visual floaters. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type II diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis. He takes aspirin, lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, and over-the-counter ibuprofen. His temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 135/82 mmHg, and pulse is 78/min. On physical examination, the right eye is firm with an injected conjunctiva and a mildly cloudy cornea. The pupil is dilated at 6 mm and is non-reactive to light. Ocular eye movements are intact. Vision is 20/200 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. The left eye exam is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
